list: the official 55 trophies, 2026-11-18 (Exophase and PSNProfiles agree)

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: The platinum is not a task of its own: it lands the moment the other 54 trophies are on your profile. Guides put the list at roughly 200 hours with no difficulty setting, no online requirement and one playthrough, since free roam continues after the credits. Watch the remaining count at the top of this tracker rather than chasing the platinum directly.
trophies.tips: Check the silver and gold rows first: 100% completion, 250 stunts and the shooting-range golds are what actually decide how long the platinum takes.
trophies.summary: Nothing here is a separate task. Every trophy below is a step of this one, so treat the platinum as a running total rather than a final errand: the count at the top of this page is the only progress bar that matters.
steps: Play the story once, on any difficulty, and keep playing after the credits — free roam is where the 100% list gets finished.
Work the golds and silvers first: A Long Road, Cunning Stunts and The Shootist decide how long the platinum takes.
Pick up Positive Mental Attitude in Chapter 1 before it closes, then stop worrying about losing anything.
Sweep the collectibles with WAiNK and the map filters, then let the platinum land with the 55th trophy.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Pops at the end of Gone Fishing, the opening mission of Chapter 1, so a fresh save earns it inside the first hour. Nothing in the mission can be failed in a way that costs the trophy. PowerPyx files it as an automatic story trophy with no other condition.
trophies.summary: Automatic and unmissable. It is the first trophy most players see on a fresh save, usually inside twenty minutes of the prologue.
steps: Start a fresh save and play the opening mission, Gone Fishing, from the prologue.
Watch for the trophy when the mission’s last cutscene ends — it needs no other condition.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Awarded for finishing Chapter 1; both PowerPyx and GTABase place the pop at the start of Chapter 2, when What's in the Bag? opens, not on the last mission of Chapter 1 itself. Nothing in the chapter can lock it out. The one thing to do first is Lucia's balcony meditation, which is only offered before this point.
trophies.tips: Make a manual save at the end of Chapter 1: this is the last moment the balcony meditation can be taken.
trophies.summary: The chapter trophy is automatic, but Chapter 1 is the only stretch of the game where something can be lost for good. Take the balcony meditation from trophy 28 before you close the chapter, then let this one pop.
steps: Take the balcony meditation (trophy 28) at some point after Down to Earth, inside Chapter 1.
Make a manual save at the end of the chapter, while the meditation is still on the table.
Play the chapter’s last mission. The trophy pops at the start of Chapter 2, when What’s in the Bag? opens.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Complete Chapter 2. GTABase puts the unlock at the start of Chapter 3, after Welcome to Vice City. Chapter 2 is also where partner free roam (Coffee Break), the Scooter Bros app and the garage property market open, so several other trophies become possible as this one lands.
trophies.summary: A chapter trophy with a chapter of its own: Coffee Break opens partner free roam, the Scooter Bros app installs and the garage market unlocks, so four other trophies become possible the moment this one lands.
steps: Play Chapter 2 through to its end.
Expect the pop at the start of Chapter 3, after Welcome to Vice City.
Use the chapter’s unlocks straight away: Coffee Break for partner free roam, the Scooter Bros app, the garage property market.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Complete Chapter 3. PowerPyx and GTABase both place the pop after the first two Chapter 4 missions, Ocean Beach and Another Life. Chapter 3 is where the Snap Gun and jewelry jobs (Yasmani), the Dye Pack Jammer for laundering and the Key Cloner strand begin.
trophies.summary: Story trophy, but Chapter 3 is the chapter that arms you: the Snap Gun for silent jewelry jobs, the Dye Pack Jammer for laundering and the Key Cloner for Randy’s car list all come from here.
steps: Play Chapter 3 through to its end.
Expect the pop a little later than the chapter itself — both PowerPyx and GTABase place it after the first two Chapter 4 missions.
Take the chapter’s tools with you: the Snap Gun for jewelry jobs and the Dye Pack Jammer for marked bills.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Complete Chapter 4. PowerPyx ties the pop to the chapter's final mission, Starting From Zero. It cannot be missed and needs no performance in the mission. Save before that last stretch if you still want to leave optional content for later.
trophies.summary: Automatic with the chapter’s last mission, Starting From Zero. Nothing in the mission has to be played a particular way.
steps: Play Chapters 4 and 5 up to the chapter’s final mission, Starting From Zero.
Finish that mission; the trophy is automatic and takes no performance.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: Finish the final story mission; it is the second of the list's two golds. GTABase notes free roam carries on after the credits, so every 100% task can be cleaned up afterwards. There is no mission replay and no trophy depends on how a mission is played.
trophies.summary: The last story trophy and one of the two golds. Free roam continues after the credits, so every 100% task can be finished afterwards — no need to stall the story.
steps: Play the story to its final mission.
Finish it. Free roam continues after the credits — nothing is closed off by finishing.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Unlocks during Breakfast Run, a Chapter 2 main mission (PowerPyx titles it as checking on Jason). Automatic once the mission ends, with no optional objective attached.
trophies.summary: A single Chapter 2 main mission, unmissable and automatic. Nothing optional hangs off it.
steps: Play the Chapter 2 main mission Breakfast Run.
Finish the mission; the trophy pops on its own.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: Unlocks during The Cartel Heist, a Chapter 3 main mission. Automatic, no extra requirement. It sits in the same chapter as the jewelry and laundering unlocks, so a story run picks it up without a detour.
trophies.summary: Automatic with The Cartel Heist, and it shares a chapter with the robbery unlocks, so a story run collects it without a detour.
steps: Play the Chapter 3 main mission The Cartel Heist.
Finish the mission; there is no optional objective attached.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Unlocks during Child's Play, the Chapter 4 main mission in which Rafa is rescued from kidnappers. Automatic, with nothing to fail beyond the mission itself, which restarts from a checkpoint if you do.
trophies.summary: Automatic with Child’s Play. If you fail the rescue, the mission restarts from a checkpoint and the trophy is unaffected.
steps: Play the Chapter 4 main mission Child’s Play.
Finish the rescue. If it goes wrong, the mission checkpoints and the trophy is unaffected.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Unlocks during Headliners, a Chapter 4 main mission built around a launch party. Automatic, and it arrives in the same chapter as the other three Chapter 4 story trophies.
trophies.summary: Automatic with Headliners. It arrives in the same chapter as the other Chapter 4 story trophies, so nothing to plan around.
steps: Play the Chapter 4 main mission Headliners.
Finish the launch party mission; the trophy is automatic.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: Unlocks during VCIA Takedown, a Chapter 4 main mission. Automatic. It has nothing to do with the airport plane trophy Catch Me If You Can beyond sharing the airport as a location.
trophies.summary: Automatic with VCIA Takedown. Despite the airport setting it has nothing to do with the plane trophy Catch Me If You Can.
steps: Play the Chapter 4 main mission VCIA Takedown.
Finish it. Nothing here relates to the separate plane trophy at the same airport.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Unlocks during Operation Savage Glory, a Chapter 5 main mission. Automatic, and one of the last story trophies before the final-mission gold, so it marks the end of the story stretch of the roadmap.
trophies.summary: One of the last story trophies before the final-mission gold: when it pops, the story stretch of the roadmap is nearly done.
steps: Play the Chapter 5 main mission Operation Savage Glory.
Finish it. From here the only story trophy left is the final-mission gold.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: Reach 100% on the in-game list under Progress > Stats > 100% Completion, which appears once the story is done; progress made during the story already counts, and nothing on it can be missed. It is not true 100%: required in full are all robberies (8 bank vaults, 39 gang operations), the underwater discoveries, all 42 shooting-range golds, all 42 drone races and Bret's 15 Target Decks, while only a share of the rest counts: 100 optional missions, 200 of 277 vehicle scans, 100 of 255 animal studies, 15 of 18 meditations, 70 of 80 challenges, 300 stunts and 100 WAiNK scans.
trophies.tips: Do the required-in-full categories first; they are also the ones that carry their own trophies. Use the in-game checklist, not this tracker, as the authority for the last few percent.
trophies.summary: This is the long one and the reason a platinum run is measured in hundreds of hours. The in-game list appears once the story is done, but everything you did during the story already counts towards it — you are only filling in the gaps.
steps: Finish the story first: the 100% list appears under Progress > Stats > 100% Completion once the credits roll.
Clear the categories required in full — all bank vaults and gang operations, the underwater discoveries, all 42 shooting-range golds, all 42 drone races and Bret’s 15 Target Decks.
Top up the partial ones: 300 stunts, 200 of 277 vehicle scans, 100 of 255 animal scans, 100 of 255 WAiNK scans, 15 of 18 meditations, 70 of 80 challenges, 100 optional missions.
Check the in-game list for the last few percent — it is the authority, not this tracker.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Complete any 250 of the 397 stunts: 130 stunt jumps, 202 under-the-bridge fly-unders, 40 knife flights and 25 base jumps. Flying under bridges in a helicopter or plane is the fastest way to add numbers, and the optional challenge attached to each stunt is not needed. The 100% checklist wants 300, so this trophy arrives on the way to A Long Road.
trophies.tips: Track the count under Progress > Activities > Stunts and turn the stunt spots on in the map filter.
trophies.summary: Twenty-five short hops is not much, but the ride is the point: stunt jumps and fly-unders are scattered next to the collectibles you will be picking up anyway, so borrow them as you travel.
steps: Fly under bridges with a helicopter or plane: 202 of the 397 stunts are fly-unders and they add numbers fastest.
Fill in with the 130 stunt jumps, the 40 knife flights and the 25 base jumps as you travel between other objectives.
Track the count under Progress > Activities > Stunts and turn stunt spots on in the map filter.
Stop at 250 for the trophy; the 100% list wants 300.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try all nine activity types once: fishing, hunting, golf, a shooting range, pool, basketball, an arcade game, winning a race and a stunt. Progress > Activities lists each type with its count, and the map's Activities filter shows what is nearby. Most types are introduced by the story, so this usually fills itself.
trophies.summary: Every one of the nine activity types is introduced by the story, so this usually fills itself while you chase other trophies. What it needs is breadth, not skill: one round of golf counts as much as a gold medal.
steps: Play one fishing session, one hunt, one round of golf, one shooting range, one game of pool and one basketball game.
Win one race and land one stunt.
Finish any one arcade game at a cabinet — the home TV covers this one early.
Check Progress > Activities: every type should show a count of at least one.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn gold in every Shooting Range challenge: 42 golds spread over 12 ranges. Golds reward accuracy and speed, so learn a range's target order on a first run and retry for time. Range practice also raises Focus, which helps with Gunslinger.
trophies.tips: Nine of the 42 are usually the last: keep the range's own score screen open and restart instead of leaving the building.
trophies.summary: Forty-two golds is the hardest activity requirement in the list after the stunts. Accuracy first, speed second: learn a range’s target order on a slow run, then retry for the clock.
steps: Pick a shooting range off the map and learn each challenge’s target order on a slow, accurate run.
Retry for the clock from the range’s own score screen — leaving the building costs a reload.
Nine of the 42 golds are usually the last, so clear a range completely before moving on.
Range practice also raises Focus, which is what Gunslinger needs.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at each of the 14 locations. One win per location is enough for the trophy, but the 100% checklist wants all 42 drone races, so clear every race at a location in one visit. Locations appear as the map unfogs.
trophies.summary: Fourteen locations, one win each — but the 100% list wants all 42 races, so clear every race at a location in a single visit rather than flying back later.
steps: Wait until the map unfogs enough to show drone-race locations; fourteen of them hold races.
Win one race at each location for the trophy.
Clear every race at a location in the same visit — A Long Road wants all 42, and flying back is wasted time.
Pick a drone you have upgraded for handling rather than speed.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races out of the 40 on the map; winning the same race twice does not count towards the twenty. Combine it with Top Fun by taking a drone race at each location, and pick short routes over long ones.
trophies.summary: Twenty different races leaves twenty spare, so pick short street and drone routes over anything long. Repeats do not count, which is the one thing to watch.
steps: Open the map’s race filter and pick the shortest routes first: street races and drone races both count.
Win twenty different races. Repeats are the trap — a second win on the same route does nothing.
Combine the two: taking a drone win at each location feeds this trophy and Top Fun at once.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: After meeting Cal in the Chapter 1 mission Feng Shui, he texts a purple fishing marker; play his fishing strand and beat him in the challenge. Fishing is a timing minigame, so wait for the bite before reeling. GTABase notes the strand stays open after the story, so a lost challenge costs nothing.
trophies.summary: A short strand that only opens once you have met Cal, and one minigame with a timing window. Nothing can be failed permanently: the strand stays on the map after the story.
steps: Meet Cal in the Chapter 1 mission Feng Shui; he texts you a purple fishing marker afterwards.
Play through his fishing strand to the challenge.
Beat him: fishing is a timing minigame, so wait for the bite before reeling rather than holding on early.
If you lose, the strand stays on the map after the story — nothing is lost.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Finish any one of the four arcade cabinets: Tenebrae Lux, Street Trash III, Time Jackers Rewind or Bang For Your Buck. The first three are on the TV at Jason and Lucia's home and playable from Chapter 1; the fourth is on cabinets out in Leonida. Finishing means reaching the end of the game, not setting a score.
trophies.summary: The cheapest trophy on the list if you start early: an arcade cabinet stands in the starting home, and finishing any of the four games is enough.
steps: Use the arcade cabinet in Jason and Lucia’s home — Tenebrae Lux, Street Trash III and Time Jackers Rewind are all there.
Pick the shortest of the three and play it to the end; reaching the end is what counts, not the score.
Put the controller down mid-game if you like: the cabinet keeps a save.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Andy's five jobs are Lucia-only and start in Chapter 3, when she gets his call and the Belville address. The order is Climbing the Cellerichain, Pay the Cellerica Fee, Peach!, Read the Label and Puff Puff Pass, and the last one awards the trophy. All five stay on the map in free roam, so the strand cannot be closed off.
trophies.summary: Andy’s jobs are Lucia-only and start in Chapter 3. All five stay on the map in free roam, so the only reason to hurry is to get it off the clean-up pile.
steps: Wait for Andy’s call and the Belville address in Chapter 3 — the five jobs are Lucia-only.
Work them in order: Climbing the Cellerichain, Pay the Cellerica Fee, Peach!, Read the Label, Puff Puff Pass.
Finish Puff Puff Pass — that is the trophy. The markers stay on the map in free roam, so nothing is lost by waiting.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Kenton, the green KR marker in Key Lento, hires Jason in Chapter 1 to recover treasure from seven shipwrecks: dive at the purple chest markers and dig with the metal detector. He goes quiet after Chapter 1 and texts again later, so the strand is finished after the story. Progress > Collections > Kenton's Treasures tracks the seven.
trophies.summary: Seven dives, seven chests. The strand goes quiet after Chapter 1 and picks up again later, so treat it as clean-up work rather than a chapter task.
steps: Start with Kenton at the green KR marker in Key Lento in Chapter 1 to open the treasure strand.
Dive at the seven purple chest markers and dig with the metal detector.
He goes quiet after Chapter 1 and texts again later — finish the last wreck then. Progress > Collections > Kenton’s Treasures tracks the seven.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Billy's five jobs are marked at the Thrillbilly Mudclub in Kelly County once Coffee Break in Chapter 2 is done, and the fifth, Hometown Heroes, is the one that awards the trophy. The strand stays available after the credits, so it needs no special timing.
trophies.summary: Five jobs at the mudclub once partner free roam opens. There is no timing pressure at all; the trophy is the fifth job and nothing else.
steps: Finish Coffee Break in Chapter 2 so the mudclub markers appear.
Play Billy’s five jobs at the Thrillbilly Mudclub in Kelly County.
Finish the fifth job, Hometown Heroes — that is the trophy.
No timing pressure: the strand is still there after the credits.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Finish eight qualifying stranger strands anywhere in Leonida. GTABase counts Kirk, Kyle, Yago and Pilot Pete as qualifying and the Moses, Tyrone, Yasmani, Andy, Billy and Eddie lines as not counting, so pick strangers rather than contacts. The trophy's own counter in the trophy list is the reliable check on progress. None of it is needed for 100%, and the strands stay open after the story.
trophies.summary: A counting trophy rather than a story one: it is the type of strand that matters, not how far into the story you are. Eight is not many once you know which contacts count.
steps: Target strangers rather than story contacts. Kirk, Kyle, Yago and Pilot Pete count; Moses, Tyrone, Yasmani, Andy, Billy and Eddie do not.
Play those strands to their end — a full strand, not a single mission.
Use the trophy’s own counter in the trophy list as the check, since the in-game map does not label the difference.
Eight is enough, and none of it is needed for 100%, so run it as clean-up.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Randy's Wish List opens after the Chapter 3 mission Clonin' Keys, Makin' GS, which also gives you the Key Cloner. Deliver the 16 sports cars on his list to his garage in west Vice City, and scan cars with WAiNK to see whether they are on it; hotel driveways around Vice Beach and Ocean Beach are the best hunting grounds. Better condition pays more but is not required.
trophies.summary: Sixteen cars, and WAiNK does the hard part for you: scanning a car tells you whether it is on the list before you spend time stealing it.
steps: Finish the Chapter 3 mission Clonin’ Keys, Makin’ GS for the Key Cloner and Randy’s Wish List.
Scan a car with WAiNK to see whether it is on the list before you steal it.
Hunt the hotel driveways around Vice Beach and Ocean Beach; that is where the sports cars cluster.
Deliver all 16 to the garage in west Vice City. Condition pays more, never the trophy.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: A Jason-only strand: after Here, Kitty Kitty in Chapter 3, Tyrone marks synthetic labs around Vice City in purple. Destroy the labs, and his last job, Shut Down the Labs, awards the trophy. It stays available after the story.
trophies.summary: A Jason-only strand with a handful of labs to destroy. The last job is the trophy and the strand stays open after the credits.
steps: Finish Here, Kitty Kitty in Chapter 3 to open Tyrone’s strand.
Destroy the synthetic labs marked in purple around Vice City as Jason.
Finish his last job, Shut Down the Labs — that is the trophy.
The strand survives the credits, so it can wait until clean-up.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at all 18 spots across Leonida; a spot with both characters together counts twice, and the last one needs them both, which only opens up after Coffee Break in Chapter 2.
trophies.tips: A manual save before the last Chapter 1 mission turns a lost balcony meditation into a five-minute rewind instead of a second 200-hour run.
trophies.summary: The one trophy a finished run can lose — everything else waits for you after the credits.
steps: After Down to Earth in Chapter 1, follow Lucia to the balcony and accept her meditation.
Reach 18 spots; the pair count twice and the last needs both after Coffee Break in Chapter 2.
Track the total under Progress > Collections > Exploration > Meditations.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Bret Vogel texts Jason after the Chapter 2 mission Coffee Break (Lucia cannot receive it) and starts Veteran Hunted in Lummox County. Hunt the animals on his purple Target Decks with a rifle; a clean one-shot kill pays more but is not required. Which animal triggers the trophy is not settled, and all 15 Target Decks are needed for 100% anyway.
trophies.summary: A hunting strand with a trophy the community has not pinned to one animal. Since all fifteen Target Decks are needed for 100%, the careful route is to hunt all of them and let the trophy arrive on its own.
steps: Finish Coffee Break in Chapter 2 as Jason; Bert Vogel texts him and starts Veteran Hunted in Lummox County.
Take a rifle to the purple Target Decks and hunt the marked animals.
A clean one-shot kill pays more but is not required for the trophy.
Hunt all 15 Target Decks — which animal triggers the trophy is not settled, and A Long Road needs all fifteen anyway.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Complete any three Collectible Card sets; you do not need all of them. Progress > Collections shows each set's count and the cards still missing, and the cards sit in fixed spots, so a set is a short tour once the remainder is known.
trophies.summary: Three sets, not all of them. Cards sit in fixed spots, so once Progress > Collections tells you what a set is missing, a set is a short guided tour.
steps: Open Progress > Collections and pick a set that is nearly complete rather than starting from zero.
Check what each set is still missing; the cards sit in fixed spots, so the list is a route.
Collect the missing cards for three different sets.
Confirm each set shows as complete before moving to the next.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: Scan 100 WAiNK spots with the phone app: hold Up on the D-pad, then R1/RB. The pool is 31 Landmarks, 35 Curiosities, 23 Sculptures and the No Flusher tags, so any hundred count. A hundred WAiNK scans are also part of the 100% checklist, so the trophy comes first.
trophies.tips: Scanning from a car covers ground quickly, and the app marks what is already scanned.
trophies.summary: The fastest collectible trophy in the list if you scan from a moving car: Landmarks, Curiosities and Sculptures alone total well over a hundred spots, so pick the dense downtown ones.
steps: Hold Up on the D-pad and scan with R1/RB, from a car: the app marks what is already done.
Work the dense pools first — 31 Landmarks, 35 Curiosities, 23 Sculptures and the No Flusher tags.
Stop at 100; those same hundred are what the 100% list asks for.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Complete 50 of the 80 challenges; Progress > Challenges ticks the finished ones. Many complete themselves as you play, and the 100% checklist wants 70, so this arrives on the way. Ten challenges are spare, which means the slowest ones can be left alone.
trophies.summary: Fifty of eighty challenges, and most complete themselves through ordinary play. The ten spare are the slow ones, so there is no reason to touch a challenge you dislike.
steps: Play normally and let the easy challenges complete themselves — running, shooting and robberies all tick.
Check Progress > Challenges to see which types are nearly done.
Finish fifty. Ten of the eighty are spare, so leave the ones you dislike.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: Once both characters can be out together, after Coffee Break in Chapter 2, call your partner with Right on the D-pad then Triangle/Y, build a four-star wanted level and escape. It only counts after you are out of the red heat zone, and the train tunnel north of Ambrosia in Kelly County is a known place to lose helicopters. Bank vault robberies always give four stars, so the trophy often pops there by accident.
trophies.summary: Needs a partner out with you, so it waits for Chapter 2. Two ways to do it: call it in on a rampage, or let a bank vault hand you four stars and simply drive away from the helicopters.
steps: Finish Coffee Break in Chapter 2 so your partner can ride out with you.
Call your partner with Right on the D-pad then Triangle/Y.
Build a four-star wanted level. Bank vault robberies hand you four stars for free.
Escape properly: you are only clear once you are out of the red heat zone. The train tunnel north of Ambrosia in Kelly County breaks helicopter pursuit.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: With your partner along, rob three shops back-to-back while the police are still chasing you; losing the wanted level breaks the chain. The three jewelry stores in north Vice City, open after Yasmani's Jewelry Jobs in Chapter 3, are close enough to chain, and body armour and healing items make the run survivable. The trophy can lag about thirty seconds after the third shop, so rob a fourth before deciding it failed.
trophies.summary: Only the chain matters, not the loot: three shops robbed without the wanted level dropping in between. Park a fast car outside the third shop before you start.
steps: Bring your partner and pick three shops close together — the north Vice City jewelry stores are the easiest chain.
Rob them back-to-back and keep the police chasing: losing the wanted level resets the chain.
Give it thirty seconds after the third before deciding, and rob a fourth if nothing pops.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover 100 different vehicles by scanning them with WAiNK; you never have to drive them. Stand on a busy road and scan passing traffic, or sweep a car park. The 100% checklist wants 200 base models, so this comes well before A Long Road.
trophies.summary: A hundred vehicles is a scanning chore, not a driving one — nothing has to be stolen or kept. A busy road or a hotel car park will do it in a few sessions.
steps: Unlock WAiNK, then hold Up on the D-pad and scan passing traffic with R1/RB.
Park on a busy road or sweep a hotel car park; nothing has to be driven or stolen.
Scan a hundred different vehicles. The 100% list wants 200 base models, so this arrives early.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down five enemies inside one Combat Focus, triggered by clicking both sticks while aiming a firearm. Fill the Focus meter first, since eating, drinking and washing up at home raise it and Adrenaline extends the window, then use an accurate automatic rifle such as the Duke 556. Gang-operation thugs count; police, soldiers and civilians appear not to.
trophies.summary: A timing trophy: five kills inside one Focus window. Build the meter at home first, bring an accurate automatic rifle and pick gang thugs rather than police.
steps: Fill the Focus meter first — eating, drinking and washing up at home all raise it — and carry Adrenaline.
Take an accurate automatic rifle such as the Duke 556 to a gang operation; thugs count, police and civilians appear not to.
Click both sticks while aiming, then take five enemies inside the one window.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Steal a large passenger jet docked at a boarding bridge at VCIA (planes parked out on the airfield do not count), back it out, take off and fly about a kilometre clear of the airport. Gates E3 and E4 are the easy ones: drive through the airfield fence and use the door by the stairs. It is a hidden trophy, so expect no hint in the list until it pops.
trophies.summary: A hidden trophy, so the list gives you nothing. The whole thing is one stolen jet, one clean take-off, and about a kilometre of straight flying.
steps: Drive to VCIA and get onto the airfield; gates E3 and E4 have a door by the stairs.
Steal a large passenger jet at a boarding bridge — planes parked on the airfield do not count.
Back out, take off and fly about a kilometre clear of the airport.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: Steal a tank from Mile Zero Air Station, the island at the south-west edge of the map in Mariana County, where the tanks stand at the south end of the base. Drive in through the gate or use the stunt jump by the south-east entrance, then take enemies out from inside the tank until the trophy unlocks.
trophies.summary: One trip to Mile Zero Air Station, and the tank does the work once you are inside the base. Getting in is the only part that asks for anything.
steps: Travel to Mile Zero Air Station, the island at the south-west edge of the map in Mariana County.
Get inside: drive in through the gate, or use the stunt jump by the south-east entrance.
Take a tank from the south end of the base.
Shoot enemies from inside the tank until the trophy unlocks — it does not need to be a set number of kills in one streak.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Yasmani's Jewelry Jobs in Chapter 3 unlock jewelry-store robberies and the Snap Gun for silently picking alarmed doors. Use the Snap Gun on the back door rather than kicking it in, find the safe-code note in the back room and empty the safe without being spotted, since setting off the alarm voids the attempt. Richardson Jewelry & Diamonds in Vice City is the store most guides use.
trophies.summary: A stealth trophy with one hard rule: set off the alarm and the attempt is void. The Snap Gun is the tool that makes it possible, and the safe code is in the back room.
steps: Finish the Chapter 3 jewelry strand to get the Snap Gun.
Pick Richardson Jewelry & Diamonds in Vice City, the store most guides use.
Pick the back door with the Snap Gun rather than kicking it in — and never touch an alarm.
Read the safe-code note in the back room, empty the safe, and leave before anyone spots you. If the alarm sounds, the attempt is void.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Bank vaults open with the Chapter 4 optional mission That's Where The Money Is...: tail a security van to its bank and get into the vault while it stands open. The haul is too heavy for one character, so hand a bag to your partner, and since vaults always give four stars, escape on a fast bike and switch vehicles. Five of the eight vaults are enough for the trophy and all eight are needed for 100%.
trophies.tips: Yasmani sells van tips for $10,000 if a particular vault is hard to find.
trophies.summary: Five vaults is the trophy and eight is the 100% list. Vaults always generate four stars, so plan the escape before you open the door, not after.
steps: Finish That’s Where The Money Is... in Chapter 4 to open vault robberies. Yasmani sells van tips for $10,000.
Tail a security van to its bank and get in while the vault stands open.
Hand a bag to your partner — the haul is too heavy for one character — then run on a fast bike.
Five vaults is the trophy; all eight are needed for A Long Road.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Robbing a bank vault counts as robbing an armored truck as long as you then escape the heat or reach a Pay 'n' Spray, so this often arrives together with Maximum Withdrawal. Earlier in the game, box in a moving armored truck, sticky-bomb its back doors, blow them and get away.
trophies.summary: Often a freebie: a bank vault robbery that ends in an escape counts here too. The armored-truck version earlier in the game is the slower, less reliable route.
steps: The easy route: rob a bank vault and escape the heat, or reach a Pay ’n’ Spray. That counts here as well as for Maximum Withdrawal.
Earlier in the game, box a moving armored truck in so it cannot escape.
Sticky-bomb the back doors and blow them open.
Take the contents and get clear of the police before the wanted level bites.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Clear the fog from the whole map of Leonida. Flying a plane over every dark patch is the quickest method and you never need to land; the trophy tracks map discovery, not collectibles, so a handful of long flights finishes it.
trophies.summary: A discovery trophy, not a collectible one: no pickups are involved at all. Long flights over the dark parts of the map are the entire method.
steps: Fly long legs over every dark patch, coasts first, and move the map filter to unexplored.
You never have to land: map discovery is the count, not collectibles.
A handful of flights usually finishes it; repeat only if a corner stays dark.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob one illegal operation belonging to each of the nine gangs; they are the yellow map icons, many of them marked by story progress. Progress > Gangs keeps the count, and repeating a gang does not help. The 100% checklist wants all 39 operations, so this one comes on the way.
trophies.summary: Nine gangs, nine operations. Repeats do not count, so follow the yellow icons rather than re-clearing the operations you already robbed.
steps: Open the map and look for the yellow gang-operation icons.
Rob one operation belonging to each of the nine gangs. The map’s Progress > Gangs screen keeps count.
Do not repeat a gang you have already robbed from — it does not move the count.
Clear all 39 operations while you are there; A Long Road requires the full set.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Have a cocktail somewhere with a view over Ocean Beach in Vice City. PowerPyx names the Ocean View rooftop bar and an Apple Martini, drunk while standing next to the bar. It is a hidden trophy, so nothing in the list hints at the bar until it pops.
trophies.summary: A hidden trophy with a specific bar and a specific drink, and nothing else to it. A two-minute stop on the way to something else.
steps: Travel to Ocean Beach in Vice City and find the Ocean View rooftop bar.
Go up to the bar and order an Apple Martini, standing at the bar itself rather than taking it away.
Drink it with the view over Ocean Beach and the trophy pops.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Steal the blue Banshee from the vehicle showroom in the south of Vice City and drive it out through the showroom window. PowerPyx notes the car can only be taken once you have the Key Cloner from Randy's Chapter 3 strand, so finish that first. Hidden trophy, no in-game hint.
trophies.summary: Two conditions: the Key Cloner from Randy’s Chapter 3 strand, and a showroom window. Until you have the first, the Banshee is not going anywhere.
steps: Finish Randy’s Chapter 3 strand first: the Key Cloner is what makes the Banshee stealable.
Go to the vehicle showroom in the south of Vice City and find the blue Banshee.
Steal it, then drive it straight out through the showroom window.
Lose the police afterwards — the trophy pops on the smash, not on the escape.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Kingpin Bowling in Port Gellhorn is a gang operation first marked by Hit Kingpin Bowling in Chapter 2. Take all three valuables — the watch in the south-east office, the Gutterball Moreland 850 shotgun on the north-east table and the safe in the north-east hallway, which needs sticky bombs — then lose the police. The robbery takes a long time to come back, so take everything in one visit.
trophies.summary: Three valuables in one visit and then a clean getaway. This is the trophy that punishes leaving a robbery half-done, because the respawn is slow.
steps: Wait for Hit Kingpin Bowling in Chapter 2 to mark the Port Gellhorn alley as a gang operation.
Take the watch from the south-east office, the shotgun from the north-east table, then blow the hall safe with sticky bombs.
All three in one visit, then lose the police — the robbery respawns slowly.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: Max out Strength on both Jason and Lucia, visible under Jason & Lucia > Strength in the pause menu. Work out at fitness clubs from the map's Activities filter with your partner along, because training one trains the other, and after the story you can also train at home.
trophies.summary: Strength training for both characters at once, which makes it a gym errand rather than a grind. Training with a partner levels the pair together.
steps: Open the map’s Activities filter and pick a fitness club.
Bring your partner: training one character trains the other at the same time.
Work Strength to maximum on both. Watch the bars under Jason & Lucia > Strength in the pause menu.
After the story you can also train at home, which saves the drive.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: Perform 500 actions that shift your Criminal Profile; the trophy itself shows the count out of 500 when you open it. Turn on Criminal Profile notifications under Settings > UI so each shift is visible, and otherwise play normally, since robberies and fights add up quickly. Do not push the meter all the way to Irredeemable, which is permanent.
trophies.summary: Not really a task: the meter fills through ordinary crime and fighting. Turn the notifications on so you can see the count, and keep the profile short of Irredeemable.
steps: Turn on Criminal Profile notifications under Settings > UI to see each shift.
Play normally: robberies, fights and general crime all move the meter.
Keep going to 500 — and stop short of Irredeemable, which is permanent.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: The description, Second time's the charm, points to succeeding at something on a second attempt, and PowerPyx links it to the Payday Loans store from the prologue, but no guide has confirmed the trigger. Treat it as a clean-up trophy: play a full run and check the tracker afterwards before hunting it.
trophies.summary: An unresolved trophy: the description points at a second attempt and PowerPyx links it to the prologue’s Payday Loans store, but no guide has confirmed the trigger. Play the run and check the list at the end before spending time on it.
steps: Play a full run first and check the trophy list at the end; this one may arrive on its own.
If it has not, revisit the Payday Loans store from the prologue that PowerPyx links it to and try a second attempt at a robbery there.
Circle back to it last: no guide has confirmed the trigger, so it is not worth grinding before the rest of the list is done.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: This is the UFO Easter egg: on the road north-west of the Starlet Motel in Kelly County, after 2 AM and alone. A blinking car at the roadside means the event can fire; if it is not there, drive away and come back, because the spawn is not guaranteed. Follow the prompt that appears beside the car.
trophies.summary: A spawn that is not guaranteed, so plan on two or three approaches. After 2 AM, alone, north-west of the Starlet Motel, with a blinking car marking the spot.
steps: Go alone after 2 AM and drive the road north-west of the Starlet Motel in Kelly County.
Look for a blinking car at the roadside; if it is missing, drive away and come back, because the spawn is not guaranteed.
Follow the prompt beside the car.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: The description asks for a melee drive-by: knock somebody down from a moving vehicle with a melee attack. PowerPyx suspects kicking enemies from a motorcycle, and no guide has confirmed the trigger yet. Try it against gang members rather than pedestrians and check the trophy list after each attempt.
trophies.summary: A hidden trophy whose trigger is still unconfirmed: the description asks for a melee drive-by and guides suspect kicking from a motorcycle. Worth one attempt against gang members, not an evening.
steps: Take a motorcycle and pick a target — gang members rather than ordinary pedestrians.
Ride up alongside a standing enemy and use a melee attack from the moving vehicle to knock them down.
Check the trophy list after the attempt. No guide has confirmed the trigger, so one or two tries is enough for now.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Finish the Chapter 3 mission Credit Check (Meet Raul's Crew) to get the Dye Pack Jammer, then rob banks and Payday Loans and sell the marked bills to a fence; Yasmani in Vice City pays the most. The $250,000 is a running total across robberies, not one delivery. Bank vaults hand over up to $205,000 a time but only open after the Chapter 4 optional mission That's Where The Money Is...
trophies.summary: A running total across robberies, so it fills while you do Maximum Withdrawal and the gang operations. Launder with a fence rather than trying to save it up in one trip.
steps: Finish Credit Check (Meet Raul’s Crew) in Chapter 3 to get the Dye Pack Jammer.
Rob banks and Payday Loans, then sell the marked bills to a fence — Yasmani in Vice City pays most.
It is a running total, not one delivery; bank vaults can hand over $205,000 a time once they open.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend a running total of $100,000 across shops of any kind. Guns, car mods and tattoos use money fastest, with 14 mod shops, 19 Pay 'n' Sprays and the clothing and electronics stores on the map. Robberies fund it, so do it after a few scores rather than grinding a job.
trophies.summary: Spending money is the trophy, so do it after a robbery pays out: guns, car mods and tattoos burn $100,000 faster than clothes or food.
steps: Rob something first so you have the money to spend.
Burn it on the fastest-spending shops: guns, car mods and tattoos beat clothing and electronics.
Use the 14 mod shops and 19 Pay ’n’ Sprays on the map rather than one store repeated.
Check the running total; $100,000 arrives quickly once you are buying weapons and upgrades.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Buy all eight garages for sale through the Vice City Real Estate app, which installs after the Chapter 2 mission Daily Driver; the four garages the story hands you do not count. The eight cost about $160,000 together. Robberies are the quickest way to raise it, and the garages also give On the Spot its parking space.
trophies.summary: Roughly $160,000 for eight properties, which is why it belongs after a few scores rather than at the start of a run. The four garages the story gives you do not count.
steps: Finish the Chapter 2 mission Daily Driver so the Vice City Real Estate app installs.
Raise about $160,000 — robberies are the quickest way.
Buy all eight garages for sale through the app. The four the story hands you do not count towards the eight.
Keep a free space: the garages are also where On the Spot parks its registered vehicles.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: The Scooter Bros app arrives with Moses' Chapter 2 mission, and stolen vehicles are registered at his Port Gellhorn garage after a respray. At first he takes only cars without trackers; from Chapter 3 any Pay 'n' Spray can register tracked ones. Each registration costs money and needs free garage space, so use cheap cars and bikes.
trophies.summary: Ten registrations, each one costing money and a free garage space, which ties this directly to the garage-property trophy. Cheap cars and bikes keep the bill down.
steps: Wait for Moses’ Chapter 2 mission to install the Scooter Bros app.
Steal cars and register them at his Port Gellhorn garage after a respray; at first only cars without trackers.
From Chapter 3 any Pay ’n’ Spray can register tracked ones. Ten total, with cheap cars and bikes keeping the bill down.

notes: Hidden flags follow the 28 trophies PSN hides until earned (PlanetGTA6). Guides are written for this entry; each cites where its facts come from.
